title: TerraMind - Climate Risk Intelligence
content:
TerraMind builds the most accurate climate risk models available to financial institutions and corporations.

Founded in 2023 by former DeepMind climate researchers and Oxford climate scientists, TerraMind applies frontier machine learning techniques to the problem of quantifying, modeling, and predicting climate-related financial risk.

Our platform combines high-resolution physical climate models, transition risk scenario analysis, and regulatory compliance reporting into a single intelligence layer that integrates directly with enterprise risk management systems.

TerraMind's models are built on proprietary datasets spanning 40 years of climate observations, satellite imagery, and economic impact data. Our machine learning approach captures non-linear interactions between climate variables that traditional actuarial models miss -- delivering risk assessments that have been independently validated as more accurate than incumbent providers in head-to-head evaluations.

Capabilities:
- Physical risk modeling: asset-level exposure to flood, wildfire, heat stress, and sea level rise
- Transition risk analysis: portfolio impact under multiple decarbonization scenarios
- Regulatory reporting: automated TCFD, EU CSRD, and SEC climate disclosure generation
- ESG scoring: proprietary methodology combining satellite data with financial metrics
- API-first architecture for integration with existing risk platforms

Trusted by leading insurers, asset managers, and banks across Europe and North America.

Headquartered in London, UK. Backed by AIVC and Breakthrough Energy Ventures.

title: Emergency Call with Lars - BlackRock Loss Post-Mortem
author: David Okonkwo
content:
CRM Note: Emergency Call -- TerraMind / BlackRock Loss
Date: May 12, 2026
Type: Unscheduled 1:1
Meeting with: Lars Eriksson (CEO)

Context: Lars called me this morning. BlackRock chose MSCI for their enterprise-wide climate risk assessment. This was TerraMind's biggest pipeline opportunity -- would have been a $400K+ ACV deal and a transformative logo.

Post-Mortem
- TerraMind won the technical evaluation. Lars says the BlackRock data science team explicitly told them TerraMind's models were "significantly more accurate"
- But MSCI won on everything else: relationship management (they had a dedicated 5-person team on the deal), commercial flexibility (offered a 2-year pilot with favorable terms), and brand trust ("nobody gets fired for buying MSCI")
- Lars is frustrated and candid: "We had the better product and we still lost. I don't know how to fix this without someone who knows enterprise sales."
- The deal took 6 months. Lars was the primary relationship manager while also running the company. He missed follow-up meetings, was slow to respond to procurement requests, and didn't have a champion strategy
- Rebecca helped where she could but she's a COO, not a salesperson

Sales Hire Update
- Lars interviewed one of the two candidates I sent (Jennifer Walsh, ex-Salesforce VP Sales). Meeting went well but Lars hasn't made an offer
- I pushed him HARD on this. "Lars, you just lost the biggest deal in your pipeline because you don't have a sales leader. What are you waiting for?"
- He acknowledged the urgency but said he's worried about culture fit -- doesn't want someone who will turn TerraMind into a "salesy" company
- I told him directly: you need to make this hire in the next 30 days or we need to have a different conversation about the company's trajectory
- He seemed to hear it. Said he'll schedule a second interview with Jennifer this week and also meet the other candidate (Marcus Thompson, ex-Snowflake)

Runway Discussion
- Cash position: $3.5M. Burn $350K/mo. ~10 months
- Without BlackRock, the path to extending runway through revenue is much harder
- Lars broached the idea of a bridge round. Said he's been thinking about $3-5M to extend runway 12 months while the new sales leader ramps
- I told him I'd raise it internally but AIVC would need to see the VP Sales hire happen FIRST before committing to a bridge. We're not going to throw more money at a company that can't sell.
- He understood. No pushback.

My Assessment
- This is a critical juncture. The BlackRock loss isn't just lost revenue -- it's a signal that TerraMind's go-to-market is fundamentally broken
- The product is best-in-class. Amara's models are genuinely 2-3 years ahead of MSCI. But the best product doesn't always win in enterprise
- Lars needs to make the VP Sales hire NOW. Not next month. Now.
- I'm going to bring this up at the next AIVC partner meeting. We need to decide if we're willing to do a bridge and under what conditions

Follow-up: Schedule check-in with Lars in 2 weeks. Confirm Jennifer Walsh interview happened.

title: Market Research Review - Climate Risk Analytics Space
author: Elena Rodriguez
content:
CRM Note: Market Research Review -- Climate Risk Analytics
Date: April 22, 2026
Type: Internal research review
Presented to: David Okonkwo

Overview: Completed deep-dive on the climate risk analytics market to support our TerraMind investment thesis and competitive monitoring. Key findings below.

Market Size & Growth
- Climate risk analytics market estimated at $4.2B in 2025, growing 40% YoY
- Projected to reach $8B by 2028 driven by regulatory requirements
- Enterprise spend on ESG/climate data & analytics is the fastest-growing category in financial data
- Key growth drivers: EU CSRD (mandatory 2025-2026), SEC climate disclosure rules (expected 2026-2027), TCFD adoption by major asset managers

Competitive Landscape
- MSCI: Dominant incumbent. Acquired climate risk capabilities through RiskMetrics and Carbon Delta. Strength is brand, distribution, and existing relationships with every major asset manager. Weakness is model accuracy (legacy actuarial approaches) and slow product innovation
- Sustainalytics (Morningstar): Strong in ESG ratings, weaker in physical climate risk modeling. Bundled with Morningstar's broader data platform
- Jupiter Intelligence: Physical climate risk specialist. Raised $54M Series C in Feb 2026. Very focused on insurance and real estate verticals. Not a direct competitor to TerraMind's broader platform but overlaps in physical risk
- S&P Global / Trucost: Large incumbent with climate data. Breadth over depth approach
- Spectra Analytics: AI-native financial analytics platform. Currently focused on market data but their ML infrastructure could pivot into ESG/climate. Worth watching.

TerraMind's Position
- Best-in-class ML models -- validated in multiple head-to-head evaluations against MSCI and Sustainalytics
- Strong regulatory alignment (EU CSRD module shipped Q1 2026)
- Weakness: commercial execution. Pipeline is healthy but close rates are well below industry average
- NRR of 120% is excellent -- customers who onboard love the product
- 97% gross retention -- nearly zero churn

Regulatory Tailwinds
- EU CSRD: Large European companies required to report starting 2025, expanding to mid-size 2026. This is a major buying trigger
- SEC Climate Disclosure: Final rules expected 2026-2027. Will force US companies to quantify climate risk. Could be a step-change for the market
- Central bank stress tests: ECB, Bank of England, and Fed all incorporating climate scenarios into bank stress tests. Requires better climate risk data

Threats
- MSCI investing heavily in AI-powered models (announced April 2026). Gap could narrow in 18-24 months
- Jupiter Intelligence's $54M raise signals more competition in the space
- Spectra's potential entry into ESG vertical -- their ML infrastructure is strong
- Big incumbents (Bloomberg, S&P) could acquire their way into better climate models

Recommendation: TerraMind has the best technology in a rapidly growing market with strong regulatory tailwinds. The investment thesis is sound. The risk is entirely commercial execution. If they can hire a VP Sales and build a real go-to-market engine, this company could be a breakout. If they can't, they'll be a great product that gets acquired for their technology at a modest multiple.

Next steps: Share this analysis with David for the partner meeting. Update quarterly.

title: Climate Risk Analytics Market to Reach $8B by 2028 as Regulations Tighten
author: Hannah Park
content:
Climate Risk Analytics Market to Reach $8B by 2028 as Regulations Tighten

By Hannah Park | Reuters | March 12, 2026

LONDON -- The global climate risk analytics market is projected to reach $8 billion by 2028, more than doubling from an estimated $3.8 billion in 2025, according to a new report from Verdantix, as financial institutions race to comply with tightening environmental disclosure regulations.

The European Union's Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD), which began phasing in for large companies in 2025 and expands to mid-size firms this year, is proving to be the most significant demand driver. The anticipated U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission climate disclosure rules, expected to be finalized in late 2026 or early 2027, could trigger a second wave of adoption across American corporations.

"We're at an inflection point," said Dr. Nadia Rousseau, head of climate finance research at Verdantix. "Climate risk quantification is moving from a nice-to-have for ESG reports to a regulatory requirement that affects capital allocation decisions."

MSCI, the dominant provider of ESG and climate risk data to the financial sector, has been investing aggressively to maintain its market position. The company recently launched an AI-enhanced climate risk platform and expanded its coverage to over 10,000 public companies and 200,000 private assets.

Sustainalytics, owned by Morningstar, remains a strong competitor, particularly in ESG ratings that are bundled with the firm's broader investment research platform.

Jupiter Intelligence, which raised $54 million in a Series C round last month, is carving out a niche in physical climate risk assessment for the insurance and real estate sectors. Its models focus on granular, asset-level exposure to floods, wildfires, and extreme heat events.

Smaller but technically innovative players are also emerging. London-based TerraMind, backed by AIVC and Breakthrough Energy Ventures, has attracted attention for its machine learning-driven approach to climate risk modeling, which it claims offers superior accuracy to traditional actuarial methods. The company has secured contracts with several European insurers and asset managers.

"The next generation of climate risk tools will be built on machine learning, not spreadsheets," said Lars Eriksson, CEO of TerraMind. "The financial models used by incumbents were designed for a stable climate. We're building for a world where historical patterns don't predict future risk."

Analysts caution that the market remains fragmented and that enterprise buyers are still uncertain about which vendors to standardize on. Integration with existing risk management systems, data quality, and regulatory alignment will be key differentiators.

"There's a lot of noise in this market," said a senior risk officer at a major European bank, speaking on condition of anonymity. "We need providers who can deliver auditable, regulator-ready outputs, not just flashy dashboards."

title: BlackRock Selects MSCI for Enterprise-Wide Climate Risk Assessment
author: Patrick Jenkins
content:
BlackRock Selects MSCI for Enterprise-Wide Climate Risk Assessment

By Patrick Jenkins | Financial Times | May 10, 2026

BlackRock has selected MSCI as its primary provider for enterprise-wide climate risk assessment, in one of the largest contracts awarded in the rapidly growing climate analytics market.

The multi-year agreement will see MSCI's climate risk platform integrated across BlackRock's investment management operations, covering physical risk assessment, transition scenario analysis, and regulatory reporting for the asset manager's $9.1 trillion portfolio.

The deal underscores the increasing importance of climate risk quantification for the world's largest asset managers, as regulatory pressure mounts on both sides of the Atlantic. BlackRock has faced scrutiny from both climate activists who argue the firm does not do enough to address climate risk and political figures who accuse it of overemphasising environmental concerns.

"This is about rigorous risk management, not ideology," said a BlackRock spokesperson. "Understanding climate-related financial risk is fundamental to our fiduciary duty."

MSCI, which has invested heavily in upgrading its climate analytics capabilities, beat out several competitors in a comprehensive evaluation process that lasted approximately six months. The company recently launched an AI-enhanced climate risk platform with scenario modeling capabilities.

"We're honoured to partner with BlackRock on this critical initiative," said Henry Fernandez, MSCI's chairman and CEO. "Our platform provides the breadth, depth, and regulatory alignment that institutional investors require."

The contract is a significant win for MSCI in an increasingly competitive market. Jupiter Intelligence, Sustainalytics, and several smaller analytics firms were understood to have participated in the evaluation.

Analysts at Morgan Stanley estimated the contract could be worth $15 million to $20 million over its duration, making it one of the largest single climate analytics deals to date.

The climate risk analytics market is projected to reach $8 billion by 2028, driven by the EU's Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive and anticipated SEC climate disclosure requirements. MSCI's dominant market position has been challenged by a wave of technology-driven startups, but the BlackRock win reinforces the advantage that established relationships and brand trust confer in enterprise sales.

MSCI shares rose 2.3 per cent on the news.

title: MSCI Launches Next-Gen Climate Risk Platform with AI-Powered Scenario Modeling
author: Sarah Ponczek
content:
MSCI Launches Next-Gen Climate Risk Platform with AI-Powered Scenario Modeling

By Sarah Ponczek | Bloomberg | April 15, 2026

MSCI Inc. unveiled a major upgrade to its climate risk analytics platform on Tuesday, introducing AI-powered scenario modeling that the company says will significantly improve the accuracy and granularity of climate-related financial risk assessments.

The new platform, branded MSCI Climate Lab AI, represents the data provider's largest investment in climate analytics technology and is designed to address growing criticism that incumbent climate risk models rely too heavily on backward-looking actuarial methods.

"We've rebuilt the analytical engine from the ground up," said Sylvain Duroure, MSCI's global head of climate solutions. "Machine learning allows us to capture the non-linear dynamics of climate change in ways that traditional models simply cannot."

Key features of the new platform include AI-generated scenario modeling for physical and transition risks, automated regulatory report generation aligned with EU CSRD and anticipated SEC requirements, asset-level physical risk analysis for over 200,000 locations globally, and portfolio-level aggregation tools for institutional investors.

MSCI said the new platform has been in development for 18 months and involved partnerships with three academic climate research centres. The company declined to disclose the total investment but said climate analytics is now one of its largest R&D budget lines.

The launch comes amid intensifying competition in the climate risk analytics market, which Verdantix estimates will grow from $3.8 billion in 2025 to $8 billion by 2028. Startups such as TerraMind and Jupiter Intelligence have been gaining traction with machine learning approaches, and MSCI's investment is seen as a response to the competitive threat from more technically innovative players.

"MSCI clearly recognises that the market is shifting toward AI-native approaches," said Forrester analyst Dr. Kenji Watanabe. "The question is whether a large incumbent can match the pace of innovation from focused startups. History is mixed on that front."

MSCI Climate Lab AI is available immediately to existing Enterprise clients and will be offered as a standalone product starting in Q3 2026. Pricing was not disclosed but analysts expect a significant premium over MSCI's existing climate modules.

MSCI shares were up 1.8% in midday trading following the announcement.

title: Jupiter Intelligence Raises $54M Series C for Physical Climate Risk Analytics
author: Tim De Chant
content:
Jupiter Intelligence Raises $54M Series C for Physical Climate Risk Analytics

By Tim De Chant | TechCrunch | February 18, 2026

Jupiter Intelligence, the physical climate risk analytics company, has raised $54 million in a Series C round led by QIC Global Infrastructure with participation from Clearvision Ventures, Energize Capital, and existing investors including Munich Re Ventures and Ninepont Partners.

The funding brings Jupiter's total capital raised to $98 million and will be used to expand the company's global climate risk modeling capabilities, grow its team from 75 to 120 employees, and accelerate expansion into the European market.

Jupiter specialises in asset-level physical climate risk assessment, providing granular analysis of exposure to floods, wildfires, extreme heat, hurricanes, and sea level rise. Its models are used by insurers, real estate investors, and infrastructure operators to quantify the financial impact of climate change on specific properties and assets.

"Physical climate risk is no longer a future problem -- it's a present one," said Rich Sorkin, CEO and co-founder of Jupiter Intelligence. "Every major hurricane, flood, or wildfire reinforces the need for accurate, forward-looking risk assessment. We're building the standard for physical climate risk analytics."

The company claims its models have been validated against historical climate events with over 90% accuracy and cover more than 150 climate hazard variables globally. Jupiter's client base includes several of the world's largest reinsurance companies and major real estate investment trusts.

The Series C round comes at a time of rapid growth in the broader climate risk analytics market, projected to reach $8 billion by 2028. Jupiter's focus on physical risk differentiates it from broader ESG and climate analytics platforms like MSCI and Sustainalytics, though there is increasing overlap as all players expand their capabilities.

"Jupiter has carved out a strong position in physical risk, which is the segment seeing the most urgent demand from insurers and real estate investors," said Patricia Chen, a partner at QIC Global Infrastructure. "The regulatory environment is only going to accelerate this."

The funding also signals consolidation dynamics in the market. With nearly $100 million in total funding, Jupiter is well-capitalised to compete against both incumbents and other startups in the space, such as London-based TerraMind and Paris-based ClimateMetrics.
